title: Building in vitro 3D human multicellular models of high-grade serous ovarian cancer
protocol: Warm tissue and culture media in a 37°C water bath until use.
Add 10 cm³ of fresh omental tissue to a 20 mL 1:1 solution of 10× trypsin and 1× DPBS in a 50 mL falcon tube.
Place the tube containing the tissue mixture in a 37°C water bath for 20 minutes.
Gently invert the tube twice after 10 minutes and at the end of the incubation period.
Neutralize the solution by adding 20 mL of warm tissue medium.
Remove the tissue from the solution and place it into a 10 cm petri dish.
Spin down the solution in the falcon tube at 200 g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Resuspend the pellet with culture medium, leaving 2–3 mL of supernatant in the falcon tube.
Plate everything in a T75 flask or 10 cm petri dish.
Leave the mesothelial cells in this medium for at least 2–3 days to allow the cells to attach to the plate.
Remove the spent medium after 2–3 days.
Wash with 1× DPBS to remove any debris.
Add new fresh medium.
Check the quality and purity of the isolation by leaving the cells growing for at least a week.
Incubate the minced tissue and collagenase solution in a shaker at 37°C, 65 g for 30–60 min.
Mix gently the digested tissue using a plastic Pasteur pipette with the end cut off until complete dissociation of all the tissue clumps.
Filter the digested tissue using 250 μm strainers that fit into a 15 mL falcon tube.
Gently press the tissue on the filter using the plunger of a 1 mL syringe to help the filtration process.
Gently pipette 2–3 mL of filtered solution into a new 50 mL falcon tube containing 20 mL of warm tissue medium to wash inactivate any residual collagenase.
Filter the digested tissue using a 250 μm strainer.
Spin down the 50 mL falcon tube at 200 g for 3 minutes at room temperature.

Move carefully the fraction containing adipocytes (second fraction from the top) to a new 50 mL falcon tube with 20 mL of warm fresh tissue medium, without disturbing the pellet in the pink/red fraction below.
Aspirate the remaining supernatant without disturbing the stromal vascular fraction pellet.
Resuspend the stromal vascular fraction pellet in fresh culture medium and plate the cells in a flask or petri dish.
Incubate the stromal vascular fraction cells in medium for at least 2-3 days at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Remove spent medium after 2-3 days of incubation.
Wash cells with 1× DPBS to remove debris.
Add new fresh medium to the cells after washing.
Spin down falcon tube containing adipocyte fraction at 200 g for 2 minutes at room temperature.
Use a plastic Pasteur pipette to collect only the adipocyte fraction, avoiding oily top and spent bottom fractions.
Place collected adipocyte fraction in a new 15 mL falcon tube.
Repeat step of collecting adipocyte fraction until it is the only fraction present within the tube.
Leave the tube in a rack for a couple of minutes until phases separate.
Measure the volume of the adipocyte fraction.
Prepare the adipocyte gel mixture as indicated in the Methods.
Keep all components, excluding the adipocyte fraction, on ice until adipocyte addition.
Pipette gently 100 μL of solution into a 96-well plate.
Invert the tube every 30 seconds to mix the solution.
Incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 to facilitate gel polymerization.
Repeat inverting the tube approximately every four gels plated.
Incubate for at least 30 minutes until gels are solidified and yellow/white.
Carefully transfer each gel to a 24-well Corning plate containing 1 mL of adipocyte gel medium using a very small spoon or spatula.
Medium change is required every second day.
Maintain the viability and usability of the adipocyte gels for up to 24–30 days for further experiments.
Perform all steps in a laminar flow hood for setting up tri-culture and tetra-culture models.
Prepare the collagen gel mixture according to the recipe listed in the methods.
Pipette 100 μl of the collagen gel mixture into a 96-well plate.
Incubate the collagen gels for at least 1 hour in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Detach the solidified collagen gels from the 96-well plate using a small spatula or spoon.
Transfer the collagen gels to a 24-well plate with 1 ml of culture medium.
Change the medium every second day.
Optionally, add a 50 μg/mL ascorbic acid solution in the medium every second day to increase ECM production by fibroblasts and malignant cells.
After 5-7 days of incubation, incorporate collagen gels into adipocyte gels.
Gently move an adipocyte gel from the culture plate to the bottom of a 24-well plate without medium.
Quickly place a collagen gel on top of the adipocyte gel.
Press the collagen gel gently within the adipocyte gel using the plunger of a 1 ml syringe.
Add 1 ml of culture medium to the well containing the embedded gels and use for further experiments.
Plan to use adipocyte gels accordingly after 21 days, as viability decreases below 50-60%.
Prepare a collagen “adhesive” solution following the recipe in the above "Materials and equipment" section.
Use the collagen adhesive solution to stick the adipocyte gel to the bottom of a 96-well plate prior to adding cells.
Move adipocyte gels from a 24-well plate to a 96-well plate on a layer of "adhesive" solution (20 μL).
Incubate the plate for at least 5 min at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Aspirate the spent medium from an 80%-90% confluent flask of fibroblasts and wash with 1× DPBS followed by trypsin.
Count the fibroblasts and plate the appropriate number (4×10^4 cells) in 100 μL of culture medium on top of the adipocyte gel.
Incubate for 2 h, then wash with 1× DPBS, trypsinize, and count the mesothelial cells.
Plate an appropriate number of mesothelial cells (2×10^5 cells) in 100 μL culture medium on top of the adipocyte gels with fibroblasts.
Incubate for 24 h at 37°C, 5% CO2 before proceeding to the next step.
Aspirate off the spent medium from the tetra-culture and wash with 1× DPBS after 24 h.
De-attach and count the malignant cells.
Carefully remove the supernatant on the adipocyte gels and replace it with 200 μL of HGSOC cells in culture medium.
Incubate the gels for 24 h at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Gently dislodge the tetra-culture and move to a new 24-well plate with 1 mL of culture medium.
